content:
Reddit made major changes to its user interface in 2018, sparking widespread protests from users who preferred the original design. The company has kept access to the old interface at old.reddit.com, and pledged last year that the legacy version would remain as long as people were still using it.

Reddit says it plans to make changes to old Reddit to block AI data scraping, a promise that now appears to be under threat to some degree...

Changes are coming to old Reddit

Reddit has already made significant changes to combat AI, introducing account verification processes. But the company now says more needs to be done, and those changes will affect old Reddit.

The news announcement was brief and vague, only mentioning that the first change would require users to log in before using the site, and hinting that moderators will be required to use new AI.

Beyond that, however, it's unclear what other changes users who insist on sticking with the old interface will face. CEO Steve Huffman promised last year that old Reddit wouldn't disappear, but how much of it ultimately survives remains to be seen.

AI moderation tools continue to expand

Reddit also announced it will adopt more AI moderation tools to help combat spam, abuse and rule violations, while expanding the test of its automated Rules Hub.

The platform says this approach is likely to be more effective than older automated moderation tools that rely on exact keyword matching.
